title: Add INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ/AWQ) into CI calibration and accuracy guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Integrate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles produced by GPTQ and AWQ into the CI calibration workflow and automated regression tests. The goal is to ensure we can safely deploy weight-only int8 variants across our serving fleet with measurable accuracy regressions and deterministic calibration artifacts. This ticket covers profile ingestion, deterministic seeding for calibration runs, storage of per-layer statistics, and automated gating in nightly and per-PR pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline accepts and runs GPTQ and AWQ-derived INT8 profile artifacts
Calibration runs are deterministic given a seed and dataset identifier
Per-model accuracy delta vs float baseline is captured and compared to thresholds
Regression job fails CI when accuracy regression > 0.5% on golden eval set or when generation quality metric drops below threshold
Profiles are versioned and linked to model/catalog entries for traceability
implementation_notes: Add new CI step `quant:calibrate-int8` that imports profile tarball and runs calibration on a trimmed eval subset
Store per-layer clip histograms and min/max ranges to object storage with retention policy 90 days
Re-use existing simulation harness for token-level generation tests but run in sample-limited mode to reduce cost
Support both GPTQ and AWQ profile formats; provide a converter shim if artifact field names differ
Ensure runtime can read profile metadata: model_version, quant_backend, seed, dataset_hash
Emit provenance metadata to CI job logs and link to artifact S3 path
test_plan: Unit: parser tests for GPTQ and AWQ profile shims
Integration: run `quant:calibrate-int8` in CI against 3 small models (base, mid, large) and compare to float baseline
Regression: nightly run across expanded eval suite; fail if any model exceeds configured regression thresholds
Canary: mark successful profiles with a `ci:passed` tag and promote to canary-serving group for 24 hours
Performance: ensure calibration step completes within configured budget (wall time < 60m for trimmed subset)
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Spike completed to parse AWQ profile format; found field `quant_axis` vs `axis` mismatch — added shim mapping
2025-02-15: Prototype `quant:calibrate-int8` job added to CI; validated deterministic seed on local run
2025-02-18: Storage layout for per-layer histograms defined (bucket: s3://redwood-quant-profiles/{model}/{version}/{profile_id})
2025-02-22: Integration test runs against small Llama-7B equiv completed; delta = 0.3% on golden prompts
2025-02-26: PR opened to add gating rules and threshold config to CI controller (ref: PR #4521)
review_feedback: PM (Jules Park): request to include targeted eval prompts that reflect customer telemetry (chat completions and code)
Design (Rina Gomez): recommend storing a condensed human-readable report alongside histograms for quick review
SRE (Omar Nassar): ensure CI step runs on isolated runners to avoid noisy-neighbor perf variance
Security (L. Huang): confirm profile artifacts are scanned for PII before retention — added to follow-up task
risks_mitigations: Risk: nondeterministic calibration due to unresolved randomness in backend. Mitigation: force seed propagation and record RNG state in profile metadata.
Risk: AWQ/GPTQ divergence in produced scales causing runtime mismatch. Mitigation: add compatibility tests and a conversion layer that normalizes scale sign/axis semantics.
Risk: CI noise causes false positives. Mitigation: run on isolated runners and require two consecutive nightly failures before blocking release branch.
rollback_plan: If CI fails after profile rollout, automatically mark latest profile as `ci:failed` and revert serving assignment to previous float/quant variant
Notify on-call and product owners; open post-mortem if regression affects customer-facing SLAs
Provide a fast path to re-run calibration with expanded eval set and increased sample size for root-cause analysis
